deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is a heavily corrected draft of the introductory paragraphs, apparently Riemann's own announcement (Selbstanzeige, Göttinger Nachrichten 1857), of his 1857 memoir 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen'. The title line at the top reads '[Beiträge] zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen'.

The prose content, through many crossed-out attempts, is as follows.
(a) The memoir treats functions which have recently found very numerous applications in mathematical physics.
(b) Gauss's investigations of the series contain applications, only part of which have been published.
(c) A remark on nomenclature: for series in which the quotient of two consecutive terms is a rational function of degree m of the index ('Stellenzeiger'), 'Herr [name not securely legible]' has proposed the name 'hypergeometric series of order m'.
(d) The Gaussian series is then characterized by its term ratio, which is the only formula on the page.

With t_n denoting the (n+1)-st term:
- t_0 = 1
- t_{n+1}/t_n = (α+n)(β+n) / ((n+1)(γ+n)) · x

Modern form (my notation): t_n = (α)_n (β)_n / ((γ)_n n!) · x^n, so F(α,β,γ,x) = 2F1(α,β;γ;x).

Since the ratio is a quotient of polynomials of degree 2 in n, Riemann remarks: 'Sie ist also nur eine hypergeometrische Reihe zweiter Ordnung' in the proposed terminology. The adjacent text contrasts this with the simpler case, in which the ratio is an integral (polynomial) function of the first degree of the index. The next page continues this sentence, stating that the name 'hypergeometrische Reihe' was originally given to that simpler series. The point is a terminological clarification for the announcement of the memoir.
errors: No mathematical errors. The term ratio (α+n)(β+n)x/((n+1)(γ+n)) with first term 1 is correct for 2F1.
Minor ambiguity: whether 'm-th degree' refers to numerator and denominator degree; under the stated convention the Gauss series is of order 2, consistent with Riemann's remark.

results.what: Definition of the Gauss series F(α,β,γ,x) by its consecutive-term ratio (α+n)(β+n)x/((n+1)(γ+n)) with first term 1
results.modern_name: Gauss hypergeometric series 2F1(α,β;γ;x) as a series with rational term ratio

results.what: Nomenclature remark: series whose term ratio is a rational function of degree m of the index are called 'hypergeometric series of order m'; the Gauss series is of second order
results.modern_name: Generalized hypergeometric series pFq (classification by term ratio)
results.usually_credited_to: Terminology of the 1840s-50s (proposer named on the page not securely legible; possibly Heine); later Thomae, Pochhammer

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known announcement of Riemann's 1857 hypergeometric memoir. The only mathematics is the standard term-ratio characterization of 2F1 plus a terminological remark. Its interest is philological (drafting history, bibliographic attribution of terminology), not mathematical.

checkable.sympy: n,a,b,c,x=symbols('n a b c x'); t=lambda k: rf(a,k)*rf(b,k)/(rf(c,k)*factorial(k))*x**k; simplify(combsimp(t(n+1)/t(n)) - (a+n)*(b+n)*x/((n+1)*(c+n)))
checkable.asserts: Term ratio of the Gauss series equals (α+n)(β+n)x/((n+1)(γ+n)) (should simplify to 0)
First term of the series equals 1
Expansion 1 + a*b/c*x + a(a+1)b(b+1)/(2c(c+1))*x**2 + ... consistent with the ratio rule

transcription_corrections: Line 1 should begin '[Beiträge] zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen' (title of the 1857 memoir).
'Die Abhandlung ist eine Ueberarbeitung [?] von Functionen gewidmet' is more plausibly 'Diese Abhandlung ist einer Classe von Functionen gewidmet' (cf. the published Anzeige).
The name of the person proposing 'hypergeometrische Reihe m-ter Ordnung' ('Herr Heine [?]') is not securely legible and should remain marked uncertain.
'n+1^{sten} Gliedes in das folgende' is correct: the ratio is the following term divided by the (n+1)-st term, i.e. t_{n+1}/t_n with first term t_0 = 1.
'zweiter Ordnung' in the lower lines refers to the Gauss series being a hypergeometric series of second order under the proposed nomenclature.
